_comment: Field recordings, rendered on demand rather than stored. `bed` names the ambient texture (see web/lib/audio.ts — the east-wing 'hum' keeps the exact spectral signature the notes describe: ~92 Hz fundamental, 0.16 Hz swell, moving 470/1180 Hz formants). `clips` place spoken lines, generated once by `npm run fetch:voices` into filesystem/assets/audio/voice/, at their real timecodes, so what you hear lines up with the transcripts. `at` is seconds from the start.

af.style: an 84-year-old Nova Scotian man, ex-longshoreman, slow and warm, a little breathy, wandering; pause where the punctuation says so

wc.style: a woman of 31, quiet and careful, speaking gently so as not to interrupt; close to the microphone

aide.style: a night care aide, brisk and kind, slightly off-microphone

papa.style: a Spanish-Canadian man in his fifties in a kitchen, amused, half-shouting at a radio, warm

mama.style: a woman in her fifties, Spanish accent, fond and exasperated, off to one side of the room

clips.text: You'll want to sit where you can see the door. Always sit where you can see the door.
I will. Can you tell me about the boats?
Which boats. There's forty years of boats.
I bought the first one off a fella named Doucette. Gerry. We were friends then.
We were friends a long time actually. On and off.
You load salt in February, your hands stop being hands. They're just... hooks.
You get the boat in, you get the lines, and somebody's wife has the kettle on, and that's the whole of it. That's the whole of a life, if you're lucky.
Is Bernadette in yet? She said she'd bring the good coffee.
Not yet.
She's always late. Fifty years late.
Don't tell her I said.
The seagulls at Pier 21 were fat as ministers.
Derek runs it all now. He won't listen. Never did.
You're good with that fishing rod. Very still. Most people fidget.
Recording. It's Wednesday, the fourteenth. How are you feeling today, Alden?
Like a man who's been sat in a chair too long. Where's the young fella with the camera?
Just me today. Is that alright?
Better. He fidgets. You don't fidget. Good girl for the fishing rod.
Ask me about the strike. Everybody wants the strike.
You cold in here? They keep it like a fridge. Bernadette hated the cold. Valencia girl. She said Canada was a mistake God made on purpose.
Tell me about her.
She waited up. Fifty years, she waited up.
The leaves are going. You can smell it. October smell.
October's a bad month. Always been a bad month.
Why's that?
You came back.
You came back. I knew you'd come back to the water. You always liked the water.
I'm here.
Gerry said don't, Gerry said just drive her home, but you were laughing at us, you had that ring on, your mother's ring, the little red stone, and Gerry got — he got the way he gets —
wasn't supposed to. Nobody was supposed to. It was the car, it was so small, and then you were quiet and that was worse, the quiet was worse than the
We went out past the yacht club. Past the tower. You know the tower. The stone one.
The Dingle.
The Dingle. Yes. It's deep off the rocks there, deeper than people think, we knew because we fished it. And your coat was so green.
You still had the ring on. I didn't take it. People say we took things. We didn't take anything.
Fifty years I've walked past that water. Derek learned to swim off those rocks and I stood on the shore and I couldn't —
Your mother called every October. Bernadette used to say, that poor woman. She never knew she was married to — she never knew.
Derek doesn't know. You have to understand that. It was me and Gerry and Gerry's in the ground.
Are you cold? You look cold. Colleen. You look so cold.
I'm alright.
Tell your mother I'm sorry. Will you tell her? Tell her he's sorry.
Alright Alden. Alright my love. Nice and easy now.
Is the tide in? I like to know if the tide's in.
I'll find out for you.
Mind the door.
Pero qué haces, hombre. Qué haces. You had him! You had him wide open!
Ramón. La radio. Los vecinos.
The neighbours agree with me, Lucía. Ask them.
Ay. Ay ay ay. No, no, no.
Wren. Wren, are you recording this? Don't record me shouting, nena.
Put it on the table. Come and eat something.
Bueno. Está bien. It's only hockey.
It is not only hockey.
Cómete la sopa antes de que se enfríe.
Fifty-one years I watch this team. Fifty-one.
